fieldMarks: Small to medium cottontail, 28–37 cm long; females slightly larger than males
Evenly dark coat of steel gray, black and orange above, white below
Fairly small ears with a slight point
behavior: Mainly crepuscular: emerges after sunset and is active into early morning, rarely in the afternoon
Rarely goes more than a few metres from dense brush, using cleared runways into grassy feeding areas
Thumps its feet when frightened, freezes for long periods, and flees in a zig-zag; may climb into shrubs when pursued
habitat: Dense scrub, chaparral, bramble thickets and brushy edges, including brush on sand dunes; seldom uses burrows.
range: Pacific coast from the Columbia River (Oregon–Washington border) south, west of the Cascades, Sierra Nevada and deserts, through much of California to Baja California. In Oregon it occupies the Willamette and other interior valleys and the coast.
